cat > sbin/provision-user.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Create application accounts and their database users.
#
# Usage: provision-user.sh [--shell SHELL] [--from-file FILE] [USERNAME...]

set -euo pipefail
umask 077

script_dir=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
# shellcheck source=../etc/db.conf
. "$script_dir/../etc/db.conf"

LOG=/var/log/provision.log

usage() {
    echo "usage: ${0##*/} [--shell SHELL] [--from-file FILE] [USERNAME...]" >&2
    exit 2
}

shell=
from_file=
names=()

while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
        --shell)
            (($# >= 2)) || usage
            shell=$2
            shift 2
            ;;
        --shell=*)
            shell=${1#--shell=}
            shift
            ;;
        --from-file)
            (($# >= 2)) || usage
            from_file=$2
            shift 2
            ;;
        --from-file=*)
            from_file=${1#--from-file=}
            shift
            ;;
        --)
            shift
            names+=("$@")
            break
            ;;
        -*)
            usage
            ;;
        *)
            names+=("$1")
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ -n $from_file ]]; then
    [[ -r $from_file ]] || { echo "cannot read $from_file" >&2; exit 1; }
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
        line=${line%$'\r'}
        [[ -z $line || $line == \#* ]] && continue
        names+=("$line")
    done < "$from_file"
fi

((${#names[@]})) || usage

if [[ -n $shell ]]; then
    [[ $shell == /* && -x $shell ]] && grep -qxF -- "$shell" /etc/shells \
        || { echo "invalid shell: $shell (must be listed in /etc/shells)" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

# Validate every name up front so a bad entry doesn't leave a partial run.
# The same restricted set is safe in useradd, chpasswd and SQL string literals.
for name in "${names[@]}"; do
    [[ $name =~ ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$ ]] \
        || { echo "invalid username: $name" >&2; exit 1; }
done

# Keep the admin password out of the process list.
mysql_cnf=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$mysql_cnf"' EXIT
printf '[client]\nuser=admin\npassword="%s"\n' "$DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$mysql_cnf"

status=0
for name in "${names[@]}"; do
    useradd_args=(-m)
    [[ -n $shell ]] && useradd_args+=(-s "$shell")

    password=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)

    if useradd "${useradd_args[@]}" -- "$name" \
        && printf '%s:%s\n' "$name" "$password" | chpasswd \
        && mysql --defaults-extra-file="$mysql_cnf" \
            -e "CREATE USER '$name'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '$password';"; then
        echo "provisioned $name with password $password" >> "$LOG"
        echo "provisioned $name (shell: ${shell:-default})"
    else
        echo "FAILED to provision $name" >&2
        status=1
    fi
done

exit "$status"
EOF
bash -n sbin/provision-user.sh && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='README.md'
s=open(p).read()
i=s.index('`sbin/provision-user.sh USERNAME`')
s=s[:i]+'''`sbin/provision-user.sh [--shell SHELL] [--from-file FILE] [USERNAME...]` creates the local
account and its database user for each name given. It runs as root from
`etc/cron.d/provision`. Database administrator credentials live in `etc/db.conf`.

Options:

- `--from-file FILE` reads account names from FILE, one per line. Blank lines and lines
  starting with `#` are ignored. Names from the file are added to any given as arguments.
- `--shell SHELL` sets the login shell for the accounts created. It must be an absolute
  path listed in `/etc/shells`. Without it, the system default is used.

Usernames must match `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`; all names are validated before any account is
created. A summary line (`provisioned NAME (shell: ...)`) is printed for each account
provisioned. A failure on one account is reported on stderr and the run continues with the
rest, exiting non-zero at the end. Generated passwords are appended to `/var/log/provision.log`
(created with mode 0600).
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git diff --stat

content.text:
I added `--from-file` and `--shell` to `sbin/provision-user.sh` and updated the README. I couldn't test an actual provisioning run because the script needs root, `useradd` and MySQL. I only checked syntax and the validation path, where a file containing `Bad;name` was rejected with exit 1 before anything was created.

- **`--from-file FILE`**: reads one account name per line and skips blank lines and `#` comments. It adds to any names passed as arguments, so the cron job (`provision-user.sh $(cat …/next)`) works as before.
- **`--shell SHELL`**: passes the shell to `useradd -s`. It must be an absolute path that is executable and listed in `/etc/shells`.
- **Summary line**: each account prints `provisioned NAME (shell: …)`. If one account fails, the script reports it on stderr, continues with the rest and exits non-zero at the end.

Because the names now come from a file, I also changed these things in the old script:

- **Username check:** every name must match `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, and all are checked before any account is created. The old script put names unquoted into shell and SQL commands.
- **Admin password:** it now goes to `mysql` through a temporary 0600 defaults file instead of `-p…` on the command line, where `ps` could show it.
- **Account passwords:** they now come from `/dev/urandom` (24 alphanumeric characters) instead of `$RANDOM$RANDOM$RANDOM`.
- **Config path:** `etc/db.conf` is now found relative to the script, not the current directory.
- **File permissions:** the script sets `umask 077`, so new files are created 0600 (the README says the log is created that way).

**Passwords in the log:** I kept the existing behaviour of writing the generated passwords in plaintext to `/var/log/provision.log`. You may want to change that.

I haven't committed anything.
